verifier_finding: Phase 4.1/4.2 explicitly calls for every control with type, name, properties. AccessControl exposes Type and Properties, but not a typed Name, so control identity is buried in the raw bag.
fix: Added `string? Name { get; init; }` to AccessControl with documentation noting nullability for anonymous Begin wrappers and the extractor double-emit rule. Updated remarks to acknowledge Name in the nullability statement.

location: AccessHarvester.Access/FormMetadata.cs and ReportMetadata.cs (remarks + DefaultView field doc)
verifier_finding: Remarks said promoted keys should be removed from Properties, but the DefaultView doc said consumers can still read Properties["DefaultView"]. DefaultView is a decoded label, not the raw value, so stripping the raw numeric code would reduce round-trip fidelity.
fix: Split the promotion rule into two cases: exact-value lifts (RecordSource, Filter, OrderBy) ARE removed from Properties; decoded lifts (DefaultView) are NOT removed — the raw numeric code is preserved alongside the decoded label. Documented in the type-level remarks of FormMetadata; ReportMetadata cross-references the same rule. Removed the contradictory consumer-facing sentence from the DefaultView field docs.

summary: Subform/subreport nesting docs were inconsistent across files
verifier_finding: AccessControl.Children docs said children can include 'a subform/subreport's contained design tree', but FormMetadata/ReportMetadata said subforms/subreports are extracted separately and not nested inline.
fix: Made AccessControl.Children the single source of truth: contained form/report tree is NOT inlined; subform/subreport nodes reference their target by SourceObject and Children should be null/empty on those nodes. FormMetadata.Children and ReportMetadata.Children docs now cross-reference this single-source contract instead of restating their own contradictory version.
